topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and sets expectations regarding the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational principles, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational overview of complement biology, including naming conventions, general functions, and the central role of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that initiate complement activation and lead to reaching the activation threshold on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the primary downstream effector functions through which complement clears pathogens, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that keep complement activation in check and prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations, infection risks, and autoimmune-like manifestations resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens employ specialized molecular mechanisms to counteract and evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
